# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The professional-profile spec delivers the site's primary professional inbound funnel: a wide-layout `/profile` page driven by a single MDX file (visual resume / CV) with structured frontmatter metadata, a contact section with LinkedIn and GitHub links, a bot-protected email address, a contact form that delivers messages via Resend, and a standalone `/contact` slash page that reuses the same contact components. Employers, recruiters, and collaborators land on `/profile`, assess Matthew's experience, and reach out — either directly by email or through the form.

## Alignment with Product Vision

- **Professional inbound funnel** (product.md business objective #1): `/profile` and the contact form are the main mechanism by which employers and recruiters get in touch.
- **Markdown-first content** (product principle #2): Profile body content lives in `content/profile.mdx` and is rendered by React components — no CMS, no database, edits are a markdown commit.
- **Simple to maintain** (product principle #3): Matthew updates the profile by editing a single MDX file.
- **Wide and spacious** (product principle #1): `/profile` uses a wider layout than standard content pages to give resume-style content room to breathe.
- **Approachable and human** (product principle #5): The contact section uses the "Shoot me a message — I respond to every human :)" copy from product.md.
- **Accessible** (product principle #7): Form submission feedback, obfuscation interactions, and all controls meet WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes.
- **Slash pages convention** (product.md feature #8): `/contact` is a lightweight standalone page reusing the same contact components.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: MDX-driven profile page

**User Story:** As a potential employer or recruiter, I want to view Matthew's professional experience on a dedicated profile page, so that I can quickly assess his fit for a role.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a visitor navigates to `/profile` THEN the page SHALL render MDX content from a single source file at `content/profile.mdx` with frontmatter-driven metadata.
2. The Velite schema for the profile document SHALL require the following frontmatter fields: `title` (page title), `description` (meta description, distinct from `/about`'s — see Req 6), `headline` (one-line role summary displayed under the name), `location` (city, country), `availability` (string describing openness to new opportunities), `updatedAt` (ISO 8601 date). It SHALL support an optional `headshot` field (path to image, colocated with the MDX file and copied by Velite to `public/static/` per the site's image convention) and an optional `resumePdf` field reserved for future use.
3. The MDX body structure SHALL be at Matthew's editorial discretion — no required section headings enforced by the spec. (Future specs MAY add structure if needed.)
4. WHEN `content/profile.mdx` is updated and the site is rebuilt THEN the rendered `/profile` page SHALL reflect the new content with no React component changes required.
5. WHEN the profile page is rendered THEN it SHALL use the `max-w-5xl` Tailwind utility (1024px / 64rem) as its content container width — wider than the standard prose column, narrower than full-bleed. This is the concrete realization of product.md's "wide layout."
6. WHEN the profile page is rendered THEN it SHALL be a statically generated server component (no per-request rendering).
7. WHEN the profile page is rendered THEN its `<title>` and meta description SHALL come from the MDX frontmatter, composed through the site-wide `%s | matthew-field.ca` title template defined in `src/app/layout.tsx`.
8. WHEN headings appear in the profile MDX body THEN they SHALL render with anchor IDs (via the existing rehype-slug convention) so that `/profile#experience`-style deep links work.
9. WHEN the build runs THEN it SHALL fail loudly on ANY of the following conditions: (a) frontmatter schema violations (Velite), (b) MDX compile errors, (c) references to undefined MDX components, (d) render-time exceptions during static generation of `/profile`. No error class SHALL degrade to runtime SSR or a blank page.

### Requirement 2: Contact section on the profile page

**User Story:** As a visitor on the profile page, I want to see how to contact Matthew at the bottom of the page, so that I can reach out after reviewing his experience.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the profile page is scrolled to the bottom THEN the contact section SHALL display links to Matthew's LinkedIn and GitHub profiles as accessible external links with appropriate `rel="noopener"` and `aria-label` attributes. These links SHALL be server-rendered (no JS required to display or follow them).
2. WHEN the contact section is rendered THEN Matthew's email address SHALL be displayed via `react-obfuscate` (click-to-reveal) so that the plain address does not appear in the raw HTML.
3. WHEN the contact section is rendered THEN the copy "Shoot me a message — I respond to every human :)" SHALL be visible above the contact form. The page owns this tagline copy (not the form component).
4. WHEN the contact section is rendered THEN the contact form (Requirement 3) SHALL be embedded inline, not behind a modal or separate navigation step.
5. The LinkedIn URL, GitHub URL, and email address SHALL be sourced from `src/config/site.ts` (extended with a `links` object containing `linkedin`, `github`, and `email` fields). Contact components SHALL NOT hard-code these values.

### Requirement 3: Contact form submits and delivers email via Resend

**User Story:** As a visitor, I want to fill in and submit a contact form with my name, email, and message, so that I can reach Matthew without needing my own mail client.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the form is rendered THEN it SHALL include three visible fields — `name`, `email`, `message` — each with an associated `<label>`, PLUS two invisible fields for bot defense: a honeypot input (bots fill; humans do not) and a timestamp input (client-stamped at form mount, used for submission-timing check).
2. The honeypot field SHALL be hidden via `display: none` on its container AND have `tabindex="-1"`, `aria-hidden="true"`, and `autocomplete="off"` on the input itself, so that keyboard users, screen readers, and password managers do not interact with it. Off-screen positioning (e.g. `.sr-only`) SHALL NOT be used.
3. WHEN the user submits the form with valid data THEN the client SHALL POST the payload as JSON to a Next.js route handler at `/api/contact`. JavaScript is required to submit the form; the no-JS fallback is the LinkedIn/GitHub/email affordances in Req 2 (all server-rendered).
4. WHEN the `/api/contact` handler receives a request THEN it SHALL apply the following checks in order, rejecting on the first failure:
    - a. Request body size ≤ 16 KB. Oversize requests SHALL return HTTP 413 with an empty body. Next.js App Router does not cap body size by default — this cap MUST be explicit in the route handler.
    - b. Origin / Referer header matches the site's own origin. Cross-origin requests SHALL return HTTP 403.
    - c. Submission timing: `now - timestamp ≥ 1000 ms`. Submissions faster than 1 second SHALL return HTTP 200 without invoking Resend (silent bot suppression — indistinguishable from success).
    - d. Honeypot empty. Populated honeypot SHALL return HTTP 200 without invoking Resend (silent bot suppression).
    - e. Zod validation of `{ name, email, message }` with the following bounds:
        - `name`: 1–100 characters, trimmed
        - `email`: valid email per zod's `.email()`, length ≤ 254 characters (RFC 5321 envelope limit)
        - `message`: 10–5000 characters, trimmed
    - f. Validation failures SHALL return HTTP 400 with a structured JSON body of shape `{ errors: { field: string } }` so the client can display field-level error text.
5. WHEN validation passes and bot checks pass THEN the API SHALL send an email via the Resend API using the Resend sandbox sender domain as the `from` address, `siteConfig.links.email` as the `to` address, and the submitter's email as `reply-to`.
6. IF Resend returns an explicit 4xx/5xx error THEN the API SHALL respond with HTTP 502 and a JSON body `{ error: "Unable to send message. Please try again or use an alternative method." }`. No vendor detail or stack traces SHALL leak to the client.
7. IF the Resend call times out (e.g. 10s ceiling) THEN the API SHALL respond with HTTP 503 and a `Retry-After: 60` header with the same user-friendly JSON body as Req 3.6.
8. WHEN the server receives a form submission THEN it SHALL NOT persist the form data in any log, database, or external service beyond Resend itself. Submitter data is relay-only.
9. WHEN the API route is deployed THEN the Resend API key SHALL be read from a Vercel environment variable, never committed to the repo. The configured sender address, recipient address, and any Resend project/org identifiers SHALL also be environment-driven.
10. The `reply-to` header is attacker-controllable (the submitter can put any address there). This spec acknowledges the risk and does NOT add email verification. Matthew MUST treat inbound sender addresses as unverified until reply traffic confirms them.
11. WHEN CI runs THEN a Playwright smoke test SHALL mount the `/contact` page, fill and submit the form, and assert a 200 response. The test SHALL mock the Resend `fetch` call and assert the route invoked it once with the expected payload shape. (Sandbox/live Resend testing is out of scope; deferred to future work if contract drift bites.)

### Requirement 4: Accessible, non-disruptive submission feedback

**User Story:** As any user — including assistive technology users — I want clear feedback after submitting the form, so that I know whether my message was sent and what to do next.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the form submits successfully THEN the system SHALL display an inline success message as an `<h2>` with `tabindex="-1"` inside a `role="status"` region (`aria-live="polite"` implicit). The system SHALL move keyboard focus to the heading, scroll it into view if off-screen, render a visible focus ring on it, and clear the form fields.
2. WHEN the form fails server-side validation (HTTP 400) THEN the system SHALL display field-level errors using `role="alert"` on each error hint (screen readers announce cooperatively, not as an interruption), PRESERVE the user's entered values, and move focus to the first invalid field.
3. WHEN the form fails due to a server error (HTTP 502 / 503 / network failure) THEN the system SHALL display a status message in a `role="status"` region (`aria-live="polite"`), PRESERVE the user's entered values, and render a visible "Try again" button. The client SHALL NOT auto-retry; the user initiates any retry.
4. WHEN the form is submitting THEN the submit button SHALL show a loading state and be disabled to prevent double-submission; all other controls remain operable.
5. WHEN any form control is rendered THEN it SHALL have a visible label, an accessible name matching the label, and native HTML5 `required` on required fields. `aria-required` SHALL NOT be added redundantly to native required inputs. Invalid fields SHALL use `aria-describedby` to associate with their error hint.
6. WHEN the contact form is navigated by keyboard only THEN tab order SHALL be logical, focus indicators SHALL be visible on all interactive elements, and submission SHALL work with Enter from any focused input.
7. WHEN the contact form is rendered in either light or dark theme THEN all text, borders, focus rings, and error states SHALL meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and non-text UI). Verified by an `axe-core/playwright` assertion (rule: `color-contrast`) running as part of the contact-form smoke test.
8. WHEN any interactive target (button, link, form control) is rendered on a touch viewport THEN it SHALL have a minimum hit area of 44×44 CSS pixels.

### Requirement 5: Standalone `/contact` slash page

**User Story:** As a visitor who has been given the `/contact` URL directly (or who reaches it via the `/slashes` index), I want to land on a dedicated contact page with the same contact options as the profile page, so that I can reach out without scrolling through Matthew's resume.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a visitor navigates to `/contact` THEN the page SHALL render the same LinkedIn / GitHub links, obfuscated email, tagline copy, and contact form used on the profile page.
2. WHEN `/contact` is rendered THEN it SHALL use the standard content container width (the default used by other `(site)` routes), not the wider `max-w-5xl` profile container.
3. The three contact components — social links, obfuscated email, contact form — SHALL live in `src/components/shared/` and be consumed independently by `/profile/page.tsx` and `/contact/page.tsx`. Each page composes the three components directly; each page owns its own tagline copy and heading structure. There SHALL NOT be a `<ContactSection>` wrapper component and the three shared components SHALL be layout-agnostic (no width concerns; the parent page imposes layout).
4. WHEN the contact form is submitted from either `/profile` or `/contact` THEN it SHALL use the same `/api/contact` handler and behave identically (same validation, same success/error UX).
5. `/contact` registration with the `/slashes` index is owned by a future spec (spec 7 per the decomposition) and is explicitly NOT this spec's scope. `/contact` inclusion in the XML sitemap is already handled by `src/app/sitemap.ts` from site-foundation (static route enumeration) and requires no change here.

### Requirement 6: SEO disambiguation between `/profile` and `/about`

**User Story:** As a recruiter searching for Matthew, I want search engines to clearly distinguish his professional profile page from his personal `/about` page, so that I land on the page that fits my intent (resume vs. personal).

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The `description` frontmatter on `/profile` SHALL be demonstrably distinct from whatever `/about` renders (copy focused on professional experience, skills, role fit).
2. `/profile` SHALL set `<link rel="canonical" href="/profile">` to itself (via Next.js metadata).
3. If the `/about` page is live at implementation time and includes Matthew's name or professional identity, the spec SHOULD note (not require) adding a link from `/about` to `/profile`. Full `/about` content is out of scope here (owned by slash-pages spec).

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- **Contact component cohesion**: Three single-responsibility components in `src/components/shared/`:
    - `<ObfuscatedEmail />` — email display via `react-obfuscate`
    - `<SocialLinks />` — LinkedIn + GitHub links
    - `<ContactForm />` — the form, owning its own state, validation, and submission logic
  The form component renders with no required props for the happy path. Pages compose the three directly.
- **No wrapper component**: `/profile` and `/contact` compose the three shared components as siblings. There is no parent `<ContactSection>` component.
- **Layout ownership**: Layout width is imposed by the consuming page, not the shared components. The shared components render layout-agnostic markup.
- **Velite schema ownership**: This spec adds a `profile` single-document schema to `velite.config.ts`. No changes to the existing `pages` schema from site-foundation.
- **Site config extension**: `src/config/site.ts` is extended with a `links` field (`linkedin`, `github`, `email`). Contact components consume from `siteConfig.links`; LinkedIn/GitHub URLs and email SHALL NOT be hard-coded anywhere else.
- **No barrel files**: Components are imported from their own paths.
- **Server components by default**: `/profile` and `/contact` are server components; only `<ContactForm />` (stateful) and `<ObfuscatedEmail />` (react-obfuscate is client-side) are `"use client"`. `<SocialLinks />` is a server component.

### Performance

- **Lighthouse ≥ 90** on both `/profile` and `/contact` across performance, accessibility, best-practices, and SEO. Verified manually against the Vercel preview deploy on the implementing PR before merge. Falling below 90 on any category is a blocking issue. No CI gate required; enforcement is pre-merge review.
- **No layout shift** from obfuscation reveal or form state changes — the contact section reserves its vertical space up front.
- **Client JS budget**: `<ContactForm />` and `<ObfuscatedEmail />` are the only client components on these pages. No additional dependencies introduced beyond `react-obfuscate`, `resend`, and `zod`.

### Security

- **Server-side validation**: All form data validated with zod on the server before any external call — client-side validation is UX only, never trusted.
- **Layered abuse defense** (composed, all evaluated server-side before Resend is invoked):
    - Request body size cap (16 KB → HTTP 413)
    - Origin/Referer header check (cross-origin → HTTP 403)
    - Timestamp-based timing check (`<1s` after mount → silent 200, no email)
    - Honeypot field (populated → silent 200, no email)
    - Zod schema validation (invalid → HTTP 400 with field errors)
- **Known latent risk — Resend 100/day quota DoS**: An attacker with a script that passes the layered defenses above could still exhaust the Resend quota. Rate limiting via external state (Vercel KV / Upstash) is deferred per tech.md. If the funnel is exhausted, LinkedIn is the documented fallback CTA — the `<SocialLinks />` and `<ObfuscatedEmail />` components continue to work independently of Resend. Funnel outage is acceptable; the LinkedIn link is always available.
- **No form-data persistence**: Submissions are relayed to Resend and not stored on the server, in logs, or in any external service beyond Resend itself.
- **Secrets in env only**: Resend API key and any sender/recipient configuration live in Vercel environment variables.
- **CSP compliance**: The contact form and obfuscation components SHALL NOT require loosening the CSP established in site-foundation. Verified by a Playwright test case that loads `/contact` with a `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` header matching the production policy, clicks the obfuscated email to trigger react-obfuscate's runtime decode, and asserts zero CSP violation reports.
- **`reply-to` is attacker-controlled**: Documented in Req 3.10. No verification; Matthew treats inbound senders as unverified.

### Reliability

- **Graceful Resend failure**: Resend outages show a clear, retryable error with form values intact; the rest of the site (and the LinkedIn/GitHub/email affordances) continue to work.
- **CI smoke coverage**: The Playwright contact-form smoke test (Req 3.11) runs on every PR and blocks merge on failure. Resend `fetch` is mocked; real Resend contract drift is not covered (deferred).

### Usability

- **Mobile responsive**: Profile page, contact section, and `/contact` adapt gracefully from mobile to desktop — form fields stack on narrow viewports, tap targets meet 44×44 CSS px (Req 4.8), text scales.
- **Theme parity**: All pages and components render correctly in both light and dark themes with no contrast or styling regressions (Req 4.7).
- **No-JS fallback is explicit, not implied**: The LinkedIn link, GitHub link, and click-to-reveal email (well, the visible "Contact" label around it) are server-rendered and work without JavaScript. The form requires JS. The obfuscated email requires JS to reveal — this is deliberate (bot protection); no-JS users see a non-interactive label. This is an accepted tradeoff for spam protection on the primary funnel.

### Observability (reserved, not wired)

- The contact form SHALL emit a named client-side event (e.g., a `CustomEvent` or analytics-function call with a fixed identifier like `contact_submit_success`) on successful submission, so a future analytics spec can subscribe without re-instrumenting the form. The specific analytics provider is out of scope for this spec. Server-side logging, Resend webhook handlers, and end-to-end delivery heartbeats are all out of scope (future work if/when they become warranted).
